Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "on tuesday the building office called me about the parcel that had been left there because it was too large for the lobby locker. my sister lena picked it up for me in the afternoon. she was already coming to my apartment to return a casserole dish, and the office closes at five, before i usually get home from work, so she had a practical chance to collect it when i couldn't. she showed her id at the desk and signed the pickup sheet; the clerk then brought the parcel out from the back room. lena texted me that the box was dry and the tape was still closed, and she put it just inside my apartment door after she arrived.
i was relieved, i think, that she could fit the pickup into her visit, although i had worried the office might ask her to come back with some extra paperwork. she said they didn't ask for anything besides her id. i haven't opened the parcel yet, so i don't know whether everything inside is fine. the office call and lena's message are the only things i have to go on for now.", "output": "On Tuesday, the building office called me about a parcel that had been left there because it was too large for the lobby locker. My sister Lena picked it up for me that afternoon. She was already coming to my apartment to return a casserole dish, and the office closes at five, before I usually get home from work. That gave her a practical opportunity to collect it when I couldn’t. She showed her ID at the desk and signed the pickup sheet, and the clerk brought the parcel out from the back room. Lena texted me that the box was dry and the tape was still closed. After she arrived, she put it just inside my apartment door.

I think I was relieved that she could fit the pickup into her visit, although I had worried the office might ask her to come back with extra paperwork. She said they didn’t ask for anything besides her ID. I haven’t opened the parcel yet, so I don’t know whether everything inside is fine. For now, I have only the office call and Lena’s message to go on."}]
